title: Python SDK typed hydrator examples and retry guidance
creator: Lena Morales
description: Create a small, well-documented set of Python SDK patterns and runnable examples that demonstrate: (1) combining dataclasses and pydantic models for typed responses; (2) robust streaming hydration that reassembles chunked events into typed objects; (3) idempotent retry strategies for both non-streaming and streaming flows; and (4) ergonomics for users to opt into strict vs permissive parsing. Deliverables include code examples, a migration guide for existing customers, unit/integration tests, and a proposal for SDK API ergonomics for v1.26.
acceptance_criteria: A curated repo folder examples/typed-hydrators with 4 runnable examples: dataclass-first, pydantic-first, mixed-hydrator, and streaming-reassembly
Each example includes a short test harness that simulates token/chunk ordering, transient failures, and duplicate chunks
A documented retry policy guide (idempotency keys, checkpointing points for streams, backoff defaults) merged into SDK docs
Migration guide with code snippets for customers moving from untyped dict responses to the typed hydrators
Benchmarks showing parse latency overhead and memory impact for 1k to 10k concurrent streams
API ergonomics proposal reviewed and approved by SDK lead and at least one PM
All examples have unit tests and integration tests enabled in CI and passing on main branch

risks_and_mitigation: Complexity: mixing dataclasses and pydantic can produce surprising validation orders - mitigate with clear guidance and a single helper API that hides orchestration
Performance: extra parsing may add latency in hot-paths - mitigate with benchmarks and lazy hydration option
Backward compatibility: breaking surface for existing untyped users - mitigate with migration guide and opt-in API flags
Operational: stream resumes require durable resume tokens - mitigation: recommend storage patterns and short-lived tokens in examples
